user_requirements: LEGAL-DRAFT REVIEW (not an acquisition analysis). The corpus contains SPA_DRAFT.md — a draft Agreement for Sale and Purchase of Shares (Nikki Wairau Christian selling all her shares in Absolute Security Group Limited and SLS RTC Limited to Ahmad Duais for NZ$260,000: $100k at settlement 1 Aug 2026, $80k 1 Sep 2026, $80k 1 Oct 2026) — plus the two precedents it was built from (PRECEDENT_ProHost_2023.pdf, drafted by Franklin Law, and PRECEDENT_Gwin_2025.pdf) and deal_facts.txt (the agreed deal terms and the Companies Register position). Review the draft as a careful New Zealand commercial solicitor would, and produce a findings list: (1) DEAL-TERM ACCURACY — does every number, date, party, company number and payment in the draft exactly match deal_facts.txt? Flag any mismatch. (2) COMPLETENESS vs the purchaser's stated requirements — restraint from the security guarding sector, restraints around customers, and strong protections: are the restraint (cl 10), non-solicit (cl 11), confidentiality (cl 12), set-off (cl 15) and settlement-deliverable (cl 3) clauses complete, internally consistent and mutually reinforcing? Identify gaps a solicitor would add (e.g. missing definitions, restraint carve-outs, notice mechanics). (3) INTERNAL CONSISTENCY — cross-references between clauses (e.g. cl 2.3 to cl 15, cl 3.1(e) to cl 9, cl 1.2 trustee joining vs execution blocks), definitions used before defined, numbering. (4) ENFORCEABILITY RISK under NZ law — restraint reasonableness/cascading, penalty-clause risk in the set-off and default clauses, the employment release (s149 ERA), pre-emptive rights in constitutions, and anything that could be struck down or backfire. (5) PRECEDENT DELTA — anything present in the two precedents that the draft dropped and should keep, and anything in the precedents that was WISELY dropped (note the Gwin precedent contains known drafting defects, e.g. its clause 2(a) compensation-at-sole-discretion wording and forfeiture clause — do NOT recommend reinstating defective clauses). (6) PROTECTION OF THE PURCHASER given the deferred payment structure and the vendor's inside knowledge. Do not redraft the whole agreement; output a numbered findings list with severity (BLOCKER / RECOMMENDED / OPTIONAL), the clause reference, the issue, and exact suggested wording for each fix. Also list every [●] placeholder and unresolved fact that must be completed before signing.
acquirer_context: Purchaser context: Ahmad Duais is buying out his business partner across two NZ security companies he already co-owns. Deferred consideration means the purchaser needs restraints and set-off that survive scrutiny; the vendor was herself a purchaser under the Pro Host precedent so she knows the template. The parties are subject to an open regulatory process (PSPLA/CIPU) — the draft must preserve personal regulatory responsibility and must not conceal anything. The final document will be settled by solicitors; this review is the pre-lawyer hardening pass.
